title: Plane intersection
prompt: Which configuration is possible for two distinct planes in Euclidean 3D?
options: They meet at exactly two isolated points
They meet in only a finite line segment
They form an isolated shared circle
They intersect in exactly one straight line
work: Two distinct planes either are parallel or intersect along a complete straight line.
A circle or finite segment cannot be the entire intersection of two infinite planes.

title: Line-plane incidence
prompt: If a straight line contains two different points of a plane, what follows?
options: The line cannot be parallel to the plane
The plane must be perpendicular to the line
The entire line lies in the plane
The line crosses the plane at a single point
work: Any two distinct points determine a line.
The plane containing both points also contains that entire line.

title: Skew lines
prompt: Which statement about two skew lines is correct?
options: They lie on the same plane and never meet
Their distance must be zero
They do not intersect and are not coplanar
They intersect at 90°
work: Skew lines are noncoplanar and nonintersecting.
Parallel lines must be coplanar, so skew lines are not parallel.

title: Perpendicular lines
prompt: What must be established before declaring two straight lines perpendicular?
options: They never meet
They intersect at a right angle
They appear to form a right angle in a perspective drawing
They have different slopes in two different planes
work: Perpendicularity of lines requires a common intersection at 90°.
Perspective illustrations may distort apparent angles.

title: Dihedral angle
prompt: The dihedral angle between two half-planes sharing an edge is measured using:
options: The distance between arbitrary points on the two faces
A section by a plane perpendicular to their common edge
Their projected area on a horizontal plane
The angles of any triangle drawn on one face
work: Take a cross-section perpendicular to the common edge.
The two intersection rays determine the plane angle of the dihedral angle.

title: Perpendicular planes
prompt: Two adjacent walls meet at an interior dihedral angle of 90°. They are:
options: Perpendicular planes
Parallel planes
Skew planes
Coincident planes
work: A right dihedral angle describes perpendicular intersecting planes.
Distinct planes cannot be skew in the line-geometry sense.

title: Polyhedron face count — challenge 1
prompt: A convex hexagonal prism has 12 vertices and 18 edges. Determine the number of faces.
work: For a convex polyhedron, V − E + F = 2; therefore F = 2 + E − V.
Substitute the given measurements: euler faces with inputs 12, 18 gives 8 faces.
restriction: The Euler relation assumes a closed connected genus-zero polyhedral surface.

title: Polyhedron face count — challenge 2
prompt: A convex heptagonal prism has 14 vertices and 21 edges. Determine the number of faces.
work: For a convex polyhedron, V − E + F = 2; therefore F = 2 + E − V.
Substitute the given measurements: euler faces with inputs 14, 21 gives 9 faces.
restriction: The Euler relation assumes a closed connected genus-zero polyhedral surface.

title: Internal box diagonal — challenge 1
prompt: A rectangular instrument cabinet has perpendicular internal dimensions 5 m, 12 m, and 13 m. Find the straight-line space diagonal.
work: Apply 3D Pythagoras: d = √(length² + width² + height²).
Substitute the given measurements: diagonal with inputs 5, 12, 13 gives 18.384776 m.
restriction: Edges meet at right angles.

title: Internal box diagonal — challenge 2
prompt: A rectangular instrument cabinet has perpendicular internal dimensions 9 m, 12 m, and 20 m. Find the straight-line space diagonal.
work: Apply 3D Pythagoras: d = √(length² + width² + height²).
Substitute the given measurements: diagonal with inputs 9, 12, 20 gives 25 m.
restriction: Edges meet at right angles.

title: Planar section of box — challenge 1
prompt: A right prism has a rectangular base 7 cm by 11 cm. A plane cuts it parallel to its base. Find the section area.
work: Parallel cross-sections of a prism are congruent to the base; A = width × length.
Substitute the given measurements: rectangle with inputs 7, 11 gives 77 cm².
restriction: The cutting plane is parallel to the base and intersects the interior.

title: Planar section of box — challenge 2
prompt: A right prism has a rectangular base 9 cm by 13 cm. A plane cuts it parallel to its base. Find the section area.
work: Parallel cross-sections of a prism are congruent to the base; A = width × length.
Substitute the given measurements: rectangle with inputs 9, 13 gives 117 cm².
restriction: The cutting plane is parallel to the base and intersects the interior.

title: Closed square prism total area — challenge 1
prompt: A closed right square prism has base perimeter 12 m, vertical height 8 m, and base area 9 m². Find the total exterior area.
work: For a right prism: S = perimeter × height + 2 × base area.
Substitute the given measurements: prism total with inputs 12, 8, 9 gives 114 m².
restriction: The given measurements describe a square base; both end faces are included.

title: Closed square prism total area — challenge 2
prompt: A closed right square prism has base perimeter 16 m, vertical height 9 m, and base area 16 m². Find the total exterior area.
work: For a right prism: S = perimeter × height + 2 × base area.
Substitute the given measurements: prism total with inputs 16, 9, 16 gives 176 m².
restriction: The given measurements describe a square base; both end faces are included.

title: Prism capacity — challenge 1
prompt: A straight-sided reservoir has uniform polygonal cross-section of area 32 m² and length 7 m. Determine internal volume.
work: For a prism: V = base area × perpendicular length.
Substitute the given measurements: prism volume with inputs 32, 7 gives 224 m³.
restriction: Cross-sectional area is constant along the length.

title: Prism capacity — challenge 2
prompt: A straight-sided reservoir has uniform polygonal cross-section of area 45 m² and length 11 m. Determine internal volume.
work: For a prism: V = base area × perpendicular length.
Substitute the given measurements: prism volume with inputs 45, 11 gives 495 m³.
restriction: Cross-sectional area is constant along the length.

title: Skew prism volume — challenge 1
prompt: A leaning prism has base area 21 cm² and perpendicular distance 9 cm between its parallel bases. Find volume (do not use the slant edge).
work: An oblique prism retains V = base area × perpendicular height.
Substitute the given measurements: prism volume with inputs 21, 9 gives 189 cm³.
restriction: The given distance is the perpendicular separation of its bases.

title: Skew prism volume — challenge 2
prompt: A leaning prism has base area 34 cm² and perpendicular distance 6 cm between its parallel bases. Find volume (do not use the slant edge).
work: An oblique prism retains V = base area × perpendicular height.
Substitute the given measurements: prism volume with inputs 34, 6 gives 204 cm³.
restriction: The given distance is the perpendicular separation of its bases.

title: Packaging box volume — challenge 1
prompt: A rectangular electronics enclosure is 4 cm wide, 7 cm deep, and 11 cm tall internally. Find the enclosed volume.
work: For a rectangular cuboid: V = length × width × height.
Substitute the given measurements: cuboid with inputs 4, 7, 11 gives 308 cm³.
restriction: The interior is a rectangular box without internal obstructions.

title: Packaging box volume — challenge 2
prompt: A rectangular electronics enclosure is 5 cm wide, 9 cm deep, and 12 cm tall internally. Find the enclosed volume.
work: For a rectangular cuboid: V = length × width × height.
Substitute the given measurements: cuboid with inputs 5, 9, 12 gives 540 cm³.
restriction: The interior is a rectangular box without internal obstructions.

title: Closed cylinder surface area — challenge 1
prompt: A completely closed upright circular cylinder has radius 4 m and height 9 m. Calculate the area of its curved wall plus both circular ends.
work: S = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h+r).
Substitute the given measurements: cylinder total with inputs 4, 9 gives 326.72564 m².
restriction: Valid for a right circular cylinder, with both bases included.

title: Closed cylinder surface area — challenge 2
prompt: A completely closed upright circular cylinder has radius 5 m and height 12 m. Calculate the area of its curved wall plus both circular ends.
work: S = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h+r).
Substitute the given measurements: cylinder total with inputs 5, 12 gives 534.07075 m².
restriction: Valid for a right circular cylinder, with both bases included.

title: Water tank volume — challenge 1
prompt: A cylindrical storage vessel has internal radius 2.5 m and usable axial height 12 m. Determine full capacity in cubic meters.
work: Use V = πr²h for a circular cylinder.
Substitute the given measurements: cylinder volume with inputs 2.5, 12 gives 235.61945 m³.
restriction: Assumes a uniform circular section and perpendicular (axial) height.

title: Water tank volume — challenge 2
prompt: A cylindrical storage vessel has internal radius 3.5 m and usable axial height 10 m. Determine full capacity in cubic meters.
work: Use V = πr²h for a circular cylinder.
Substitute the given measurements: cylinder volume with inputs 3.5, 10 gives 384.8451 m³.
restriction: Assumes a uniform circular section and perpendicular (axial) height.

title: Oblique cylindrical vessel — challenge 1
prompt: An oblique cylindrical core has circular base radius 2 cm and perpendicular distance 11 cm between bases. Determine its volume.
work: For an oblique cylinder, V = πr² × perpendicular height.
Substitute the given measurements: cylinder volume with inputs 2, 11 gives 138.23008 cm³.
restriction: Use perpendicular height, not the tilted generator length.

title: Oblique cylindrical vessel — challenge 2
prompt: An oblique cylindrical core has circular base radius 4 cm and perpendicular distance 9 cm between bases. Determine its volume.
work: For an oblique cylinder, V = πr² × perpendicular height.
Substitute the given measurements: cylinder volume with inputs 4, 9 gives 452.38934 cm³.
restriction: Use perpendicular height, not the tilted generator length.

title: Steel pipe wall volume — challenge 1
prompt: A hollow pipe is 10 cm long, with outer radius 7 cm and inner radius 5 cm. Determine the volume of wall material.
work: Subtract inner cylindrical volume from outer volume: V = π(R²−r²)L.
Substitute the given measurements: pipe volume with inputs 7, 5, 10 gives 753.98224 cm³.
restriction: Outer radius must be greater than the inner radius.

title: Steel pipe wall volume — challenge 2
prompt: A hollow pipe is 12 cm long, with outer radius 8 cm and inner radius 3 cm. Determine the volume of wall material.
work: Subtract inner cylindrical volume from outer volume: V = π(R²−r²)L.
Substitute the given measurements: pipe volume with inputs 8, 3, 12 gives 2073.4512 cm³.
restriction: Outer radius must be greater than the inner radius.

title: Regular pyramid lateral area — challenge 1
prompt: A right regular square pyramid has base perimeter 24 m and a common triangular-face slant height of 5 m. Find lateral area (exclude base).
work: For a regular pyramid, lateral area = (base perimeter × face slant height)/2.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramid lateral with inputs 24, 5 gives 60 m².
restriction: Common slant height requires a right regular pyramid.

title: Regular pyramid lateral area — challenge 2
prompt: A right regular square pyramid has base perimeter 32 m and a common triangular-face slant height of 5 m. Find lateral area (exclude base).
work: For a regular pyramid, lateral area = (base perimeter × face slant height)/2.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramid lateral with inputs 32, 5 gives 80 m².
restriction: Common slant height requires a right regular pyramid.

title: Pyramid sand volume — challenge 1
prompt: A pyramid-shaped sand pile has flat base area 72 m² and perpendicular height 10 m. Estimate idealized sand volume.
work: Pyramid volume equals one third of base area times perpendicular height.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramid volume with inputs 72, 10 gives 240 m³.
restriction: Use perpendicular height; the pile is modeled as a perfect pyramid.

title: Pyramid sand volume — challenge 2
prompt: A pyramid-shaped sand pile has flat base area 108 m² and perpendicular height 8 m. Estimate idealized sand volume.
work: Pyramid volume equals one third of base area times perpendicular height.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramid volume with inputs 108, 8 gives 288 m³.
restriction: Use perpendicular height; the pile is modeled as a perfect pyramid.

title: Oblique pyramid — challenge 1
prompt: An irregular pyramid has polygonal base area 60 cm² and perpendicular apex-to-base height 9 cm. Compute its volume.
work: Even for an oblique or irregular pyramid, V = (base area × perpendicular height)/3.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramid volume with inputs 60, 9 gives 180 cm³.
restriction: The area provided is the complete base area.

title: Oblique pyramid — challenge 2
prompt: An irregular pyramid has polygonal base area 42 cm² and perpendicular apex-to-base height 13 cm. Compute its volume.
work: Even for an oblique or irregular pyramid, V = (base area × perpendicular height)/3.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramid volume with inputs 42, 13 gives 182 cm³.
restriction: The area provided is the complete base area.

title: Cone slant height — challenge 1
prompt: A right circular funnel cone has radius 8 cm and perpendicular height 15 cm. Find a straight generator (slant height).
work: Slant height satisfies l² = r²+h²; take l = √(r²+h²).
Substitute the given measurements: cone slant with inputs 8, 15 gives 17 cm.
restriction: A right circular cone, with apex directly over base center.

title: Cone slant height — challenge 2
prompt: A right circular funnel cone has radius 7 cm and perpendicular height 24 cm. Find a straight generator (slant height).
work: Slant height satisfies l² = r²+h²; take l = √(r²+h²).
Substitute the given measurements: cone slant with inputs 7, 24 gives 25 cm.
restriction: A right circular cone, with apex directly over base center.

title: Cone storage capacity — challenge 1
prompt: A conical vessel has circular opening radius 4 m and perpendicular depth 15 m. Determine its ideal internal volume.
work: V = πr²h/3.
Substitute the given measurements: cone volume with inputs 4, 15 gives 251.32741 m³.
restriction: Assumes a complete cone, not a frustum.

title: Cone storage capacity — challenge 2
prompt: A conical vessel has circular opening radius 6 m and perpendicular depth 11 m. Determine its ideal internal volume.
work: V = πr²h/3.
Substitute the given measurements: cone volume with inputs 6, 11 gives 414.69023 m³.
restriction: Assumes a complete cone, not a frustum.

title: Leaning cone volume — challenge 1
prompt: An off-center-apex (oblique) cone has base radius 5 m and perpendicular apex altitude 12 m. Find volume.
work: V = πr²h/3 uses perpendicular altitude even for an oblique cone.
Substitute the given measurements: cone volume with inputs 5, 12 gives 314.15927 m³.
restriction: Do not use the right-cone curved-surface-area shortcut.

title: Leaning cone volume — challenge 2
prompt: An off-center-apex (oblique) cone has base radius 3 m and perpendicular apex altitude 16 m. Find volume.
work: V = πr²h/3 uses perpendicular altitude even for an oblique cone.
Substitute the given measurements: cone volume with inputs 3, 16 gives 150.79645 m³.
restriction: Do not use the right-cone curved-surface-area shortcut.

title: Tapered vessel volume — challenge 1
prompt: A right circular conical frustum has lower radius 6 m, upper radius 3 m, and perpendicular height 8 m. Determine volume.
work: V = (πh/3)(R²+Rr+r²).
Substitute the given measurements: frustum volume with inputs 6, 3, 8 gives 527.78757 m³.
restriction: Both ends are parallel circles of a conical frustum.

title: Tapered vessel volume — challenge 2
prompt: A right circular conical frustum has lower radius 8 m, upper radius 2 m, and perpendicular height 7 m. Determine volume.
work: V = (πh/3)(R²+Rr+r²).
Substitute the given measurements: frustum volume with inputs 8, 2, 7 gives 615.75216 m³.
restriction: Both ends are parallel circles of a conical frustum.

title: Pyramid pedestal — challenge 1
prompt: A pyramid truncated parallel to the base has lower area 81 m², upper area 25 m², and perpendicular height 8 m. Find frustum volume.
work: V = h(A₁+A₂+√(A₁A₂))/3.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramidal frustum with inputs 81, 25, 8 gives 402.66667 m³.
restriction: Cross-sections are similar polygons; the cutting plane is parallel to the base.

title: Pyramid pedestal — challenge 2
prompt: A pyramid truncated parallel to the base has lower area 100 m², upper area 36 m², and perpendicular height 9 m. Find frustum volume.
work: V = h(A₁+A₂+√(A₁A₂))/3.
Substitute the given measurements: pyramidal frustum with inputs 100, 36, 9 gives 588 m³.
restriction: Cross-sections are similar polygons; the cutting plane is parallel to the base.

title: Spherical tank volume — challenge 1
prompt: A spherical tank has interior radius 5 m. What is its complete internal volume?
work: Substitute the given measurements: sphere volume with inputs 5 gives 523.59878 m³.
restriction: The cavity is a full sphere.

title: Spherical tank volume — challenge 2
prompt: A spherical tank has interior radius 7 m. What is its complete internal volume?
work: Substitute the given measurements: sphere volume with inputs 7 gives 1436.755 m³.
restriction: The cavity is a full sphere.

title: Closed hemisphere total area — challenge 1
prompt: A closed hemispherical enclosure has radius 6 m. Find its curved wall area plus its flat circular floor.
work: S = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr².
Substitute the given measurements: hemisphere total with inputs 6 gives 339.29201 m².
restriction: Total area includes the circular closure.

title: Closed hemisphere total area — challenge 2
prompt: A closed hemispherical enclosure has radius 9 m. Find its curved wall area plus its flat circular floor.
work: S = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr².
Substitute the given measurements: hemisphere total with inputs 9 gives 763.40701 m².
restriction: Total area includes the circular closure.

title: Circumscribed sphere radius — challenge 1
prompt: A cube of edge 8 cm is inscribed in a sphere (all eight cube vertices on the sphere). Determine the sphere radius.
work: Cube space diagonal = edge√3 and equals the enclosing sphere diameter; r = edge√3/2.
Substitute the given measurements: circumscribed radius with inputs 8 gives 6.9282032 cm.
restriction: Sphere passes through all cube vertices.

title: Circumscribed sphere radius — challenge 2
prompt: A cube of edge 10 cm is inscribed in a sphere (all eight cube vertices on the sphere). Determine the sphere radius.
work: Cube space diagonal = edge√3 and equals the enclosing sphere diameter; r = edge√3/2.
Substitute the given measurements: circumscribed radius with inputs 10 gives 8.660254 cm.
restriction: Sphere passes through all cube vertices.

title: Spherical cap volume — challenge 1
prompt: A plane removes a spherical cap of height 3 cm from a sphere of radius 8 cm. Calculate the cap volume.
work: V = πh²(R−h/3).
Substitute the given measurements: cap volume with inputs 8, 3 gives 197.92034 cm³.
restriction: Cap height is between 0 and 2R.

title: Spherical cap volume — challenge 2
prompt: A plane removes a spherical cap of height 4 cm from a sphere of radius 9 cm. Calculate the cap volume.
work: V = πh²(R−h/3).
Substitute the given measurements: cap volume with inputs 9, 4 gives 385.3687 cm³.
restriction: Cap height is between 0 and 2R.

title: Two-base spherical segment — challenge 1
prompt: A sphere is cut by two parallel planes 5 cm apart, yielding section-circle radii 3 cm and 4 cm. Find the enclosed spherical segment volume.
work: V = πh(3a²+3b²+h²)/6 for the two circular section radii a and b.
Substitute the given measurements: segment volume with inputs 3, 4, 5 gives 261.79939 cm³.
restriction: The two cuts bound one contiguous segment of a sphere.

title: Two-base spherical segment — challenge 2
prompt: A sphere is cut by two parallel planes 6 cm apart, yielding section-circle radii 4 cm and 5 cm. Find the enclosed spherical segment volume.
work: V = πh(3a²+3b²+h²)/6 for the two circular section radii a and b.
Substitute the given measurements: segment volume with inputs 4, 5, 6 gives 499.51323 cm³.
restriction: The two cuts bound one contiguous segment of a sphere.

title: Regular tetrahedron total surface area — challenge 1
prompt: A regular tetrahedron has all edges 5 cm long. Find total area of its four equilateral triangle faces.
work: Each face has area (√3/4)a². Four faces give S = √3a².
Substitute the given measurements: tetra area with inputs 5 gives 43.30127 cm².
restriction: All four faces must be equilateral.

title: Regular tetrahedron total surface area — challenge 2
prompt: A regular tetrahedron has all edges 7 cm long. Find total area of its four equilateral triangle faces.
work: Each face has area (√3/4)a². Four faces give S = √3a².
Substitute the given measurements: tetra area with inputs 7 gives 84.87049 cm².
restriction: All four faces must be equilateral.

title: Ellipsoidal vessel — challenge 1
prompt: An ellipsoid has three mutually perpendicular semiaxes 4 m, 6 m, and 8 m. Find its enclosed volume.
work: V = (4π/3)abc.
Substitute the given measurements: ellipsoid volume with inputs 4, 6, 8 gives 804.24772 m³.
restriction: The given distances are semiaxes, not full diameters.

title: Ellipsoidal vessel — challenge 2
prompt: An ellipsoid has three mutually perpendicular semiaxes 3 m, 5 m, and 9 m. Find its enclosed volume.
work: V = (4π/3)abc.
Substitute the given measurements: ellipsoid volume with inputs 3, 5, 9 gives 565.48668 m³.
restriction: The given distances are semiaxes, not full diameters.

title: Torus ring volume — challenge 1
prompt: A ring-shaped toroidal seal has major radius 7 cm and circular tube radius 2 cm. Calculate solid volume.
work: V = (2πR)(πr²) = 2π²Rr².
Substitute the given measurements: torus volume with inputs 7, 2 gives 552.69785 cm³.
restriction: Ring torus with major radius R strictly larger than tube radius r.

title: Torus ring volume — challenge 2
prompt: A ring-shaped toroidal seal has major radius 9 cm and circular tube radius 3 cm. Calculate solid volume.
work: V = (2πR)(πr²) = 2π²Rr².
Substitute the given measurements: torus volume with inputs 9, 3 gives 1598.8759 cm³.
restriction: Ring torus with major radius R strictly larger than tube radius r.

title: Composite solid volume — challenge 1
prompt: A vessel assembly has three disjoint chambers holding 46 L, 38 L and 15 L. Find total capacity.
work: Add the nonoverlapping chamber volumes.
Substitute the given measurements: sum with inputs 46, 38, 15 gives 99 L.
restriction: The chambers do not overlap.

title: Composite solid volume — challenge 2
prompt: A vessel assembly has three disjoint chambers holding 70 L, 25 L and 12 L. Find total capacity.
work: Add the nonoverlapping chamber volumes.
Substitute the given measurements: sum with inputs 70, 25, 12 gives 107 L.
restriction: The chambers do not overlap.

title: Bored metal block — challenge 1
prompt: A rectangular block is 12 cm by 10 cm by 8 cm. A round hole of radius 2 cm passes through its 8-cm dimension. Find solid volume remaining.
work: Vremaining = length × width × thickness − π(hole radius)²×thickness.
Substitute the given measurements: drilled block with inputs 12, 10, 8, 2 gives 859.46904 cm³.
restriction: The through-hole lies wholly inside the block.

title: Bored metal block — challenge 2
prompt: A rectangular block is 15 cm by 12 cm by 6 cm. A round hole of radius 3 cm passes through its 6-cm dimension. Find solid volume remaining.
work: Vremaining = length × width × thickness − π(hole radius)²×thickness.
Substitute the given measurements: drilled block with inputs 15, 12, 6, 3 gives 910.354 cm³.
restriction: The through-hole lies wholly inside the block.

title: Scaled prototype volume — challenge 1
prompt: A 13-liter prototype is enlarged so every linear dimension is multiplied by 2.5. What is the resulting volume?
work: For similar solids, Vnew = Voriginal × (linear scale)³.
Substitute the given measurements: scale volume with inputs 13, 2.5 gives 203.125 L.
restriction: Uniform scaling in all three spatial dimensions.

title: Scaled prototype volume — challenge 2
prompt: A 8-liter prototype is enlarged so every linear dimension is multiplied by 3. What is the resulting volume?
work: For similar solids, Vnew = Voriginal × (linear scale)³.
Substitute the given measurements: scale volume with inputs 8, 3 gives 216 L.
restriction: Uniform scaling in all three spatial dimensions.

title: Truncated cone removal — challenge 1
prompt: From a right cone with radius 6 cm and height 12 cm, remove a smaller similar tip cone with radius 2 cm and height 4 cm. Find the remaining frustum volume.
work: Subtract similar cone volumes: V = (π/3)(R²H−r²h).
Substitute the given measurements: truncated cone with inputs 6, 12, 2, 4 gives 435.63418 cm³.
restriction: The tip cone is similar and removed by a cut parallel to the base.

title: Truncated cone removal — challenge 2
prompt: From a right cone with radius 9 cm and height 15 cm, remove a smaller similar tip cone with radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. Find the remaining frustum volume.
work: Subtract similar cone volumes: V = (π/3)(R²H−r²h).
Substitute the given measurements: truncated cone with inputs 9, 15, 3, 5 gives 1225.2211 cm³.
restriction: The tip cone is similar and removed by a cut parallel to the base.

title: Revolving a rectangle — challenge 1
prompt: Rotate a rectangle of height 4 cm and length 7 cm fully about the axis along its length. Find the volume swept out.
work: The rotation produces a cylinder: V = π(radius)² × length.
Substitute the given measurements: disk with inputs 4, 7 gives 351.85838 cm³.
restriction: The axis coincides with one long side of the rectangle.

title: Revolving a rectangle — challenge 2
prompt: Rotate a rectangle of height 2.5 cm and length 9 cm fully about the axis along its length. Find the volume swept out.
work: The rotation produces a cylinder: V = π(radius)² × length.
Substitute the given measurements: disk with inputs 2.5, 9 gives 176.71459 cm³.
restriction: The axis coincides with one long side of the rectangle.

title: Cavalieri matching sections — challenge 1
prompt: Two solids of equal height 7 cm have equal horizontal sections of constant area 18 cm² at every level. Find the volume of either solid.
work: By Cavalieri, the two volumes match; each is integral of section area: V = Ah.
Substitute the given measurements: cavalieri with inputs 18, 7 gives 126 cm³.
restriction: All corresponding heights have equal cross-sectional area.

title: Cavalieri matching sections — challenge 2
prompt: Two solids of equal height 11 cm have equal horizontal sections of constant area 24 cm² at every level. Find the volume of either solid.
work: By Cavalieri, the two volumes match; each is integral of section area: V = Ah.
Substitute the given measurements: cavalieri with inputs 24, 11 gives 264 cm³.
restriction: All corresponding heights have equal cross-sectional area.

title: Earthworks prismoid — challenge 1
prompt: A true prismoid of height 8 m has end areas 100 m² and 36 m² and midsection area 64 m². Find volume by the prismoidal rule.
work: V = (h/6)(A₁+4Am+A₂). For similar linear sections, the area varies quadratically.
Substitute the given measurements: prismoid with inputs 100, 64, 36, 8 gives 522.66667 m³.
restriction: Only use for an appropriate prismoid, not an arbitrary body.

title: Earthworks prismoid — challenge 2
prompt: A true prismoid of height 12 m has end areas 64 m² and 16 m² and midsection area 36 m². Find volume by the prismoidal rule.
work: V = (h/6)(A₁+4Am+A₂). For similar linear sections, the area varies quadratically.
Substitute the given measurements: prismoid with inputs 64, 36, 16, 12 gives 448 m³.
restriction: Only use for an appropriate prismoid, not an arbitrary body.

title: Centroid volume sweep — challenge 1
prompt: A thin rectangular planar region with area 12 cm² revolves through 360° about an external coplanar axis 5 cm from its centroid. Determine swept volume.
work: Pappus volume theorem: V = area × (2π× centroid-axis distance).
Substitute the given measurements: pappus volume with inputs 12, 5 gives 376.99112 cm³.
restriction: The axis is coplanar and external to the entire region.

title: Centroid volume sweep — challenge 2
prompt: A thin rectangular planar region with area 15 cm² revolves through 360° about an external coplanar axis 7 cm from its centroid. Determine swept volume.
work: Pappus volume theorem: V = area × (2π× centroid-axis distance).
Substitute the given measurements: pappus volume with inputs 15, 7 gives 659.73446 cm³.
restriction: The axis is coplanar and external to the entire region.

title: Centroid surface sweep — challenge 1
prompt: A straight plane curve of length 14 cm revolves once about a coplanar axis 6 cm from its centroid that does not meet the curve. Find swept area.
work: Pappus surface theorem: S = curve length × (2π× centroid-axis distance).
Substitute the given measurements: pappus area with inputs 14, 6 gives 527.78757 cm².
restriction: The generating curve does not intersect the rotation axis.

title: Centroid surface sweep — challenge 2
prompt: A straight plane curve of length 9 cm revolves once about a coplanar axis 5 cm from its centroid that does not meet the curve. Find swept area.
work: Pappus surface theorem: S = curve length × (2π× centroid-axis distance).
Substitute the given measurements: pappus area with inputs 9, 5 gives 282.74334 cm².
restriction: The generating curve does not intersect the rotation axis.

title: Half-full horizontal cylinder volume — challenge 1
prompt: A horizontal right circular cylinder of radius 1.5 m and length 6 m is filled exactly to its centerline. How many liters are inside?
work: Half of full-cylinder volume = ½πr²L cubic meters; multiply by 1,000 L/m³.
Substitute the given measurements: half cylinder liters with inputs 1.5, 6 gives 21205.75 L.
restriction: The axis is horizontal and the liquid surface passes through the center.

title: Half-full horizontal cylinder volume — challenge 2
prompt: A horizontal right circular cylinder of radius 0.8 m and length 10 m is filled exactly to its centerline. How many liters are inside?
work: Half of full-cylinder volume = ½πr²L cubic meters; multiply by 1,000 L/m³.
Substitute the given measurements: half cylinder liters with inputs 0.8, 10 gives 10053.096 L.

title: Metal pipe material mass — challenge 1

title: Optimal closed-cylinder radius — challenge 1
prompt: A fully closed right circular cylinder must hold 54π cm³ while minimizing total material surface area. Find its optimal radius.
work: Minimum area occurs at h = 2r. Thus V = πr²h = 2πr³, giving r = (V/(2π))^(1/3).
Substitute the given measurements: opt radius with inputs 169.646 gives 3 cm.
restriction: Fixed volume, right cylinder, two end disks included.
